originalAlarm.description: Memory dynamically allocated by `malloc`, indirectly via call to `inet_ehash_locks_alloc()` on line 43 is not freed after the last access at line 46, column 1.

reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (KNOWN, CORRECTLY CONSTRAINED): 218ad12f42e.c (Linux inet). When CONFIG_NUMA=true, the preprocessor causes 'x = NULL' at line 37 to become the else-body of 'if (size > PAGE_SIZE) free(x); else x = NULL;' inside inet_ehash_locks_free(). When inet_ehash_locks_alloc allocates via the else-branch malloc (line 21, triggered when size <= PAGE_SIZE), inet_ehash_locks_free takes the else branch (x = NULL) without freeing the allocated memory — a genuine memory leak. The tool detects this as MEMORY_LEAK_C. The presence condition (NUMA=true) is correctly constrained: when NUMA=false, 'free(x)' and 'x = NULL' are both executed sequentially as independent statements (not conditional), so no leak occurs. The vbdb bug for this file is exactly this preprocessor-induced memory leak when NUMA=true.
